sentences.text: Hello everyone, welcome back to English for everyday life with me and me Lee.
Have you ever been to a coffee shop and felt nervous about ordering in English?
Don't worry, today I will teach you how to order coffee, ask questions, and have a smooth
conversation in English at a coffee shop. This episode is for A1 level English learners,
so I will speak slowly and clearly. By the end of this episode, you will learn how to enter and
greet the staff, how to order coffee tea and other drinks, how to customize your drink, milk, sugar,
size, etc. How to order food and ask about ingredients, how to pay and understand prices,
how to ask for Wi-Fi and a table, how to politely make small talk, so grab a cup of coffee,
sit back, and let's start learning. 1. Entering the coffee shop and greeting the staff.
When you walk into a coffee shop, you might hear a friendly greeting.
Barista, hello, welcome to coffee shop name. What can I get for you today?
Common phrases, hi, can I see the menu please? Good morning, do you have decaf coffee?
What do you recommend? Can I order here or do I need to sit down first?
Tip, some coffee shops have menus on the wall, while others have printed menus at the counter.
2. Ordering coffee or tea. Now, let's practice how to order a drink.
Common phrases, I'd like a cappuccino please. Can I get a latte? Do you have ice coffee?
I'd like a black coffee with no sugar. Can I have a tea with lemon? Hi, I'd like a cappuccino please.
Sure, what size would you like? Small, medium, or large? Medium, please.
Would you like sugar or milk? No sugar, but I'd like oat milk please.
Got it, anything else? No, that's all. Tip, many coffee shops offer different types of milk,
such as almond milk, oat milk, and soy milk. 3. Ordering food and snacks, many coffee shops sell pastries,
sandwiches, and desserts. Common phrases, do you have croissants? I'd like a chocolate muffin please.
What kind of sandwiches do you have? Can I get a cookie and a coffee? Is this gluten-free?
Example dialogue, do you have any vegan snacks? Yes, we have vegan brownies and oat cookies.
Great, I'll take an oat cookie. Tip, if you have food allergies, always ask before ordering.
For paying for your order, after ordering you need to pay. Common phrases,
how much is it? Can I pay with a card? Do you accept apple pay? Can I have the receipt please?
Example dialogue, how much is it? That will be $6.50. Can I pay by card? Sure, tap or insert your card.
Thank you. Some coffee shops don't accept cash, so it's good to have a card or mobile payment app.
5. Asking for wifi and a table. If you want to sit and work, you may need to ask about wifi
or a place to sit. Common phrases, do you have free wifi? What's the wifi password?
Is this table available? Can I sit here? Example dialogue. Excuse me, do you have wifi?
Yes, the password is on the receipt. Thanks. Tip, some coffee shops limit wifi time to one
or two hours, so check before sitting down. 6. Picking up your order and saying thank you.
When your order is ready, the barista will call your name. Capicino for Emily.
Common phrases. That's me, thank you. Excuse me, is this my order? Can I get a napkin please?
Tip, if they get your order wrong, say excuse me, I think this is incorrect. I ordered a latte,
not a black coffee. 7. Making small talk in a coffee shop. You might want to chat with the barista
or other customers. The coffee smells amazing. Do you come here often? Is this place always this busy?
This cafe has a great atmosphere. Yes, I come here every morning before work. That's nice.
What's your favorite drink here? Tip, in English speaking countries, small talk is common in coffee
shops. 8. Final tips for visiting a coffee shop. Be clearly and politely. Always say please,
and thank you. Check the menu before ordering to decide quickly. Know your drink preference.
Hot or iced? Sugar or no sugar? Dairy or non-dairy? If the shop is busy, wait in line patiently.
Be friendly. Small talk can be a great way to practice English.
That's the end of today's episode. Now you know how to order coffee and snacks in English.
Next time you visit a coffee shop, try using these phrases. If you enjoyed this episode,
